skill.name: writing-plans
skill.description: Create detailed implementation plans for multi-step development work before editing code.
skill.summary: Turns requirements into clear, test-driven implementation plans with file paths, tasks, and handoff steps.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, code fences, example file paths, and example test or git commands. remediation.issue: Markdown examples triggered external command detection.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that listed pytest and git commands are examples for generated plans, not commands the skill should run automatically.

content.value_statement: Complex development tasks often fail when teams start coding without a shared plan. This skill turns requirements into test-driven implementation plans for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Creates implementation plan documents for multi-step development work.
Breaks work into small tasks with tests, implementation, verification, and commit steps.
Specifies expected file paths, changed files, and test files for each task.
Includes example test commands and expected pass or fail results.
Adds an execution handoff section with session options after the plan is saved.
Promotes TDD, DRY, YAGNI, and frequent commits in the generated plan.
limitations: It writes planning guidance, not production code.
It depends on accurate requirements and repository context from the user.
Example commands must be reviewed before anyone runs them.
Referenced sub-skills may not exist in every assistant environment.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Build
use_cases.description: Convert a feature specification into ordered tasks with file paths, tests, commands, and commit checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Handoff
use_cases.description: Create a plan that another assistant session or developer can follow with limited project context.

use_cases.title: Structure Test-Driven Work
use_cases.description: Define failing tests, minimal implementation steps, verification commands, and expected results before code changes begin.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill to create an implementation plan for this feature: [describe feature]. Include files, tests, commands, and commit steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan From Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using an existing specification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill with this requirement document: [paste requirements]. Create a plan saved under docs/plans with small TDD tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for controlled changes across existing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill to plan this refactor: [describe current design and target design]. Include risk areas, tests, and exact files to inspect.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Session Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for work that another session will execute.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill to create a handoff-ready plan for [project goal]. Include task checkpoints, expected outputs, and execution options.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a plan to add login rate limiting.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a dated plan with a goal, architecture notes, task list, target files, failing tests, verification commands, and commit points.

output_examples.input: A lead asks for a refactor plan before changing service boundaries.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines inspection steps, test coverage tasks, minimal implementation phases, expected test results, and a final execution handoff.

output_examples.input: A developer needs another session to implement a completed specification.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a plan that explains context, exact work items, validation steps, and options for subagent or separate-session execution.

best_practices: Provide the feature specification and any relevant repository context before asking for the plan.
Review generated file paths, commands, and expected outputs before execution begins.
Keep each task small enough to test, review, and commit independently.
anti_patterns: Do not use the plan as a substitute for understanding production constraints.
Do not run generated commands blindly without checking the repository state.
Do not ask for broad plans without requirements, acceptance criteria, or target files.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It creates implementation plans that describe tests, code changes, commands, and handoff steps.

faq.question: Where does it save plans?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to save plans under docs/plans with a dated feature filename.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does it mention TDD?
faq.answer: It structures each task around a failing test, minimal implementation, verification, and commit.

faq.question: Are the commands safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Treat commands as plan examples and review them before execution.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: A clear specification, acceptance criteria, known files, constraints, and any testing requirements produce the best plan.
